result.topic_en: Euler writes the general equation for all vibratory motions of the elastic rod as a sum of modes, then in Corollary 1 evaluates the curve shape for the fundamental tone at two points to show the rod's figure differs entirely from the first case.
result.transcription:
sicque, si $\omega$, $\omega'$, $\omega''$, $\omega'''$ denotent omnes valores ipsius $\omega$, aequatio generalis, omnes motus virgae complectens, erit:
$y = C\,\text{fin.}\left(\zeta + t\frac{\omega\omega c\sqrt{2gb}}{aa}\right)$
$\left(e^{u\omega} \mp e^{\omega(1-u)} - (1 \pm e^{\omega})\,\text{fin.}\,u\omega - (1 \mp e^{\omega})\,\text{cof.}\,u\omega\right)$
$+ C'\,\text{fin.}\left(\zeta' + t\frac{\omega'\omega' c\sqrt{2gb}}{aa}\right)$
$\left(e^{u\omega'} \mp e^{\omega'(1-u)} - (1 \pm e^{\omega'})\,\text{fin.}\,u\omega' - (1 \mp e^{\omega'})\,\text{cof.}\,u\omega'\right)$
$+ C''\,\text{fin.}\left(\zeta'' + t\frac{\omega''\omega'' c\sqrt{2gb}}{aa}\right)$
$\left(e^{u\omega''} \mp e^{\omega''(1-u)} - (1 \pm e^{\omega''})\,\text{fin.}\,u\omega'' - (1 \mp e^{\omega''})\,\text{cof.}\,u\omega''\right).$
etc. etc. etc.

Corollarium 1.

§. 44. Quanquam autem omnes motus cum casu primo perfecte conueniunt: tamen figura, quam virga inter vibrandum recipit, toto coelo est diuersa. Ad quod ostendendum euoluamus figuram pro sono fundamentali, vbi est $\omega = \frac{3\pi}{2}$, cuius sinus cum sit negatiuus, signa valebunt inferiora, eritque omisso coefficiente
$y = - - - - e^{u\omega} + e^{\omega(1-u)} - (1 - e^{\omega})\,\text{fin.}\,u\omega - (1 + e^{\omega})\,\text{cof.}\,u\omega,$
vbi est $e^{\omega} = 111$. Nunc autem ipsi $\omega$ tribuamus duos valores $\frac{1}{3}$ et $\frac{2}{3}$, ac reperiemus:
I. Si $u = \frac{1}{3}$, $u\omega = \frac{1}{2}\pi = 90^\circ$ et $e^{u\omega} = 4,8104$ et $e^{-u\omega} = 0,2079$
hincque $y = 4,8104 + 23,0769 + 110 = 138$.
II. Si $u = \frac{2}{3}$, erit $u\omega = \pi = 180^\circ$ et $e^{u\omega} = 23,140$ et $e^{\omega(1-u)} = 4,810$,
hincque $y = 23,140 + 4,810 + 112 = 140$. Hi autem duo valores, si calculum accuratius instituissemus, prodiissent aequales. Curua igitur, quam virga hoc casu induit, habebit figuram $ErsF$, fig. 4 repraesentata. Pro sequentibus
[margin: Tab. III. Fig. 4.]

items.quote: Quanquam autem omnes motus cum casu primo perfecte conueniunt: tamen figura, quam virga inter vibrandum recipit, toto coelo est diuersa.
items.english: Although all the motions agree perfectly with the first case, yet the figure which the rod takes while vibrating is entirely different.

items.quote: Hi autem duo valores, si calculum accuratius instituissemus, prodiissent aequales.
items.english: These two values, had we carried out the calculation more accurately, would have come out equal.
